answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits confirm fabricated work. A lantern-style public log links each stake to its job history, while a forge cannot cheaply mint more identities because each new account needs fresh locked collateral. The vine of Sybils therefore multiplies the attacker’s capital at risk, and one proven fraud can erase the stake behind that identity.
